source.title: LRTuner: A Learning Rate Tuner for Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Nikhil Iyer; V. Thejas; Nipun Kwatra; R. Ramjee; Muthian Sivathanu

record.tranche_reason: The study reports held-out performance alongside training loss and argues that its learning-rate method can generalize badly without an added explore phase; its experiments compare that method with hand-tuned schedules. It does not test memorization of arbitrary labels or most claim versions directly.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own test metrics and training losses for LRTuner and baseline schedules. These bear on V4's optimizer comparison only where the tested optimizer and conditions match that version; the reported Adam and momentum results are comparisons between schedules, not between adaptive and non-adaptive optimizers. Its discussion of minima width and large-batch generalization cites prior work and is not a result of this study.
record.test_reason: The study uses the premise that wider minima generalize better to motivate LRTuner's explore phase, then evaluates its own learning-rate schedules. It tests none of V1–V8: adaptive and non-adaptive optimizers are never compared on the same workload, batch size is not varied, and magnitude-aware sharpness is not measured.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately captures the authors' conclusion: LRTuner approximately matched or exceeded baseline held-out performance and sometimes reached baseline scores sooner. They report training-step reductions of 29% on ImageNet, 20% on SQuAD, and 24% on IWSLT, while acknowledging remaining tuning hyperparameters.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces an adaptive learning-rate schedule that fits a local quadratic to loss samples, with explore and exploit phases; comparisons use hand-tuned baseline schedules. It does not reproduce the original sources' interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors state that adding an explore phase significantly helped generalization; results also vary across task/model schedule comparisons, with an almost unchanged Cifar-10 test accuracy and improved scores on ImageNet, SQuAD and IWSLT.

fits_no_version.finding: LRTuner gives ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 76.06 versus 75.87, CIFAR-10 accuracy of 94.79 versus 94.81, SQuAD EM of 81.2 versus 80.7, and IWSLT BLEU of 34.88 versus 34.70.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed learning-rate tuner approximately matches or improves held-out performance against the tested hand-tuned schedules.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors state that greedy local learning-rate reductions can generalize badly and that adding an explore phase helped; they provide no controlled explore-phase ablation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An initial high-learning-rate explore phase can improve generalization of a greedy local learning-rate tuner.

record.problems: No experiments test arbitrary-label fitting, network width, architecture comparisons, explicit regularization comparisons, sharpness measures, or memorized-example removal. Most reported comparisons concern the proposed learning-rate schedule versus a baseline, not whether training loss predicts held-out error. The abstract and introduction make generalization claims more broadly than these experiments establish.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width needed to interpolate.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD or momentum SGD performance on matched workloads, including tuning, weight-decay, and switching conditions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and remedies for large-batch penalties.
Dropout effects and their dependence on training-set size, dropout strength, and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The large-batch findings are cited background. The wide-minima premise motivates the method but does not establish V7's specific magnitude-aware correlation. The superbatch-size experiment measures variance in loss estimates, not generalization under different training batch sizes.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fitting or natural-label generalization comparison.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD or momentum SGD on the same task; Adam is evaluated on NLP tasks and SGD with momentum on image tasks, with learning-rate schedules varied.
No batch-size comparison or fixed-epoch large-batch penalty test.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or competing generalization-measure comparison.
No removal of memorized examples or retraining comparison.
